correctness.rationale: Let coalition imbalance d_C=a_C-b_C. For opposite-sign imbalances C,D, the sum of gains for an A-agent moving C→D and a B-agent D→C is (q+1)(d_C-d_D)-2q>=2. Since all imbalances sum to zero, any unbalanced partition has a profitable move. For balanced per-type blocks k, current utility q+(1-q)k, joining block l yields (1-q)l and singletons yield 0: exact iff conditions q<1 spread <=q/(1-q), q=1 all, q>1 max k<=q/(q-1). Labeled block counting gives (m!)^2 divided by ∏ c_j!(j!)^(2c_j). Quadratic welfare identity S_C=q s_C+(1-q)s_C²/2-(1+q)d_C²/2 gives global optimum; squared-block allocation gives worst equilibrium, and zero-welfare iff q=k/(k-1), integer k>=2 dividing m. Independent exact direct-deviation checks for m=2,3 and q=1/2,1,4/3,2,5/2 agreed; infinite m and real q follow from algebra.
